text:
amanda: ran a quick nsys + perfetto pass on the repro for the 2nd-stage perf regression. attaching timeline and a short log. noticed weird gaps around the KV prefetch path :thinking_face:

amanda: tl;dr: there are ~3-5 small NVTX ranges per request that look like 'prefetch-shadow' — they sit between decode/kernels and push the kernel selector into a slower path.

amanda: perf log snippet:
```
[INFO] request=abcd123 model=gpt-xxx seq=128 batch=1 kernel=matmul_fast runtime_us=620 prefetch_us=18
[INFO] request=abcd123 prefetch-shadow_us=42 kernel_switch_us=110 -> fallback=matmul_generic runtime_total_us=852
```

sanjay: hmm do you mean these are NVTX ranges you added or something generated by the runtime?

amanda: runtime emits small NVTX ranges for prefetch attempts right now. they were meant to be lightweight but they show up in the timeline and correlate with kernel_selector path changes.

bryan: can you paste the exact NVTX names? we should standardize naming if we're going to sample them.

amanda: current names I saw: `prefetch_attempt`, `kv_fetch_wait`, `prefetch-shadow` (the last one is ad-hoc from an older patch).

eva: yikes `prefetch-shadow` is the one we added months ago as a debug span. agreed we should normalize. suggestion: `kv_prefetch.attempt`, `kv_prefetch.wait`, `kv_prefetch.shadow`? dot-separated helps perf parsers.

liam: +1 on dot-separated. also we should ensure spans have request_id and kernel_hint tags so traces can join with nsys kernel timeline events.

amanda: I attached perfetto link: https://perfetto.local/r/1777770001 (private) — look at the vertical kernel lanes; you can see the selector switching after those tiny spans.

infra-bot: perf artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/1777770001/nsys.trace, perfetto/1777770001.json

sanjay: quick experiment idea — collapse those tiny spans into a single `kv_prefetch` parent per request and mark child timing as metrics only (no NVTX) to reduce selector noise. if kernel selector sees fewer boundary events it may pick stable kernels.

bryan: agreed but we need to be careful — we rely on fine-grained spans for debugging. maybe runtime can emit NVTX only above a threshold (>= 1ms) and otherwise record internal counters.

eva: thresholding sounds good. Also propose canonical span naming rules (for eng-runtime):
- prefix: `rv.` for runtime (e.g., `rv.kv_prefetch.attempt`)
- separators: `.` not `-` or `_`
- suffixes: `.start` / `.end` avoided — use duration-only ranges
- include tags in NVTX name: `rv.kv_prefetch.attempt;r=request_id;l=seq` (semi-colon kv style)

liam: tiny nit: embedding tags into the NVTX string helps human read but bloats range names. we should push metadata via perfetto counters or event args instead of cramming into name.

amanda: noted. for now I propose a short name + perfetto event args. e.g. `rv.kv_prefetch.attempt` + args {request_id, kernel_hint, seq_len}.

sanjay: about kernel selector — I pulled a kernel timeline and noticed selector calls spike right after `kv_fetch_wait`. looks like the selector re-evaluates when any NVTX boundary closes. maybe our selector subscribes to NVTX callbacks.

bryan: it's probably the fallback path calling `choose_kernel()` synchronously after cache miss. we can debounce selector calls per-request to avoid churn.

eva: debounce sounds safe. put a 0.5ms coalesce window per-request and make it configurable. add metric for how often debounce flips kernels.

amanda: next steps I can: 1) rename spans in a small PR, 2) add thresholding (emit NVTX only if > 1ms) 3) attach perfetto args instead of long names. want review before I push.

sanjay: +1 review. also please add a short repro script that hits KV prefetch hot-path with/without NVTX so we can run A/B nsys.

bryan: I'll add a small trace postmortem to the perf board after amanda's run. include before/after kernel timelines. :thumbsup:

amanda: thanks all — I'll open PRs and ping this thread with the A/B traces when ready.
